diagnostic_evidence.root_cause_confirmed: The accumulated fragment buffer rode INSIDE the uplb flow marker as base64url JSON (cf:uplb:<label>:<b64token>); that marker lives in the receiving-indicator Telegram message text, capped at 4096 UTF-16 units. A multi-KB paste pushed the marker past the cap, Telegram rejected the indicator send/edit (message is too long), the sendForceReply choke point never fired so awaiting_input stayed at upl (empty buffer), and the next bare bubble parsed the trailing fragment ALONE -> Unexpected token. join('') itself and the post-1bfb0eb raw capture were byte-perfect; the defect was marker-carried state exceeding the message-size ceiling (the contract's prime suspect, confirmed).

fix.what_was_actually_wrong: Buffer stored in the Telegram-message-carried uplb marker (base64 of all fragments) — exceeded the 4096-char message cap on multi-KB plans, breaking the awaiting_input re-anchor. FIX: new D1 table plan_upload_buffer (migration 0003) + storage helpers put/get/deletePlanUploadBuffer; keepPlanPasteAlive persists the buffer to D1 first and uses a constant-size marker cf:uplb:<label>:<fragCount>:<millis> (tiny but changing per fragment — a constant payload was eaten by deleteAwaitingInputIfUnconsumed, caught by ground-truth A2/B3); uplb case reads the buffer from D1 (legacy b64 arg tolerated/ignored); buffer deleted on success, validation failure, and size overflow.
